surfaces.part: gray-blue cap/roof over the sign board
brown sign board with white 'cafe' lettering (vertical face)

answer.evidence: Rows 1-6 form a gray-blue cap that overhangs the board (width 12 to 16 against 14 for the body). A highlight sits in rows 2-4. The cap ends in a darker front-edge line at row 7, then a dark outline/eave row at row 8. Below that, rows 9-30 are the brown board face with lettering, 22 rows tall. No side face is drawn. The cap is rounded only at its upper corners (widths 8, 12, 16) and has no narrowing at the bottom, so it is not a true ellipse. It still reads as a top plane because of the edge line and shadow below it. This is a borderline call. The board itself is a flat front elevation, and the top band is the only horizontal surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small vertical sign with a brown/orange body, a darker cap and a Korean-text panel. It measures 11 visible tones per tile, which is above bus-shelter-a (6) and close to kiosk-a (12), though below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills (bus-shelter-a has 9%). Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted dark brown, matching the references' material-tone outlines. The shading ramp is a little shallower than the kiosk and vending references (about 4 steps against 5), but it is similar to the shipped modern_city props at the same scale. A careful artist would accept it beside them without it looking flatter or more sticker-like.

surfaces.part: top cap / hood of the sign

answer.evidence: The main body is the brown board in rows 9-30, a flat vertical face with white lettering and no horizontal surface. The grey-blue cap in rows 0-7 widens 8, 12, 16 and then sits flat on the narrower 14-wide board. That makes it a rounded hat or cornice, not an ellipse. Its pale highlight in rows 2-4 is a front-facing gloss. Row 7 is slightly darker and row 8 is the dark outline, so there is no clear receding top plane. Nothing in the drawing shows depth, so I read it as a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small vertical sign with a brown body, a cap, and light Hangul lettering. By the numbers it holds up: 11 visible tones per tile against 6 (bus shelter), 12 (kiosk) and 20 (vending), 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted and not a black sticker line. By eye, the body ramp is only about 3-4 steps (highlight edge, mid, dark, deep), against roughly 5 on the kiosk and vending machine. The wood face is mostly smooth with little grain or speckle, and the lettering is the main detail. The piece is narrow and sparse, so I do not penalise the density fact. It sits between the bus shelter and the richer references. It is not obviously thinner or flatter than the bus shelter, but it is a bit plainer than the kiosk and vending machine. When in doubt, fail.
